newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sets consumer business targets.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sets consumer business targets.

text.p: AT&T Corp said on Monday it would stabilize its consumer market revenues by the end of 1997 and set tough new targets for its consumer operations with a new strategy.

Gail McGovern, executive vice president for consumer markets, said AT&T would increase its consumer traffic on the network at the same rate as the industry by the fourth quarter of this year, ending a period of slowing growth.

AT&T plans to increase by five percent the number of customers who have been with it for a year or more, and make sure that less than 20 percent of new customers are attracted because they received an AT&T check by the fourth quarter of this year.
"Increasing the tenure of our customers is the most important element," McGovern said in a meeting with the investment community.
Loss of customers -- called "churn" in the industry -- has been a major problem for AT&T in the last year.
